subject: Paget papers (PP MS 4/02): letters from George Stepney, 1693-94, and the unlisted sub-series 01-25
body:
Dear [RECIPIENT NAME],

I run a small non-commercial project that reads cipher passages in historical letters. I send every message myself; the searches of the catalogues and printed editions, and the checks, are done by AI agents (Claude models) working in an open repository, where every step is logged.

My question is about the papers of William, 6th Baron Paget (PP MS 4), and specifically whether they hold the letters George Stepney wrote to Paget in 1693-94, in Paget's first year as ambassador at Constantinople. Stepney's own letter-book copies are at The National Archives (SP 105/60), and your collection record's "Associated material" note points there (SP 105/58-60). Several of those copies mention cipher (the catalogue also marks cipher words in ff.123 and 138); two concern us most: SP 105/60/121 (17/27 November 1693), which acknowledges a letter from Constantinople, "cover given in cipher", and SP 105/60/135 (addressed, in the catalogue's words, "To [? Paget]"), the concluding part of a 1694 letter with a postscript in cipher, whose key the TNA cataloguer records as untraced in SP 106. The copy Paget received, if it survives, might carry a deciphering in another hand.

What we have done that concerns your holdings: we read the online catalogue of PP MS 4/02 (Correspondence to William Paget, 1684-1707, "58 sub-series"). On 8 October 2026 the series tree showed sub-series 26 to 64 only; the records for 01 and 13 answered "Page not found", so we could not tell whether sub-series 01-25 exist under those numbers or what they contain. None of the titles we could read names Stepney, and the files we opened (27/01 and 28/01, "50 letters mostly 1693-4") are described only at file level. The likeliest place we can see is 47, "Misc letters arranged alphabetically by sender". Our notes and the catalogue tables we made are here: https://github.com/NoAutopilot/cipher-lab/tree/main/ciphers/sp105-paget-1693

Could you tell me (1) whether PP MS 4/02/47, or any other part of the Paget papers, holds letters from George Stepney of 1693-94, and if so under which reference; and (2) what sub-series 01-25 of PP MS 4/02 are, if there is a list or handlist not shown online? If Stepney letters are there, I would then ask separately about the conditions for reference images of the one or two that matter.

If the catalogue rendering of 01-25 is simply a display fault on our side, I am sorry to have raised it.

With thanks,

[SIGN-OFF]
